record_notes.DCP-LETT-360A: Government support request in Covington hand, authored by Darwin. Presidents endorsements are distinct from Darwin prose. Initiates request through Beaufort, no incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-366F: Northern vegetation and frozen ground questions follow a Richardson visit. Government petition remains pending. Postmark and Monday support July24; later printed outcomes do not backfill answers.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-370F: Acknowledges missing Richardson climate letter and anticipated visit. Unofficial grant news arrived this morning, distinct from later formal approval. No surviving climate response text identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-468: Suggestions on describing Australian valleys, prompted by drawing/personal communications of uncertain medium. Broad1838 date; no extant letter pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-415: Asks Royle lecture place and time after hearing of it. Prospective attendance differs from later notebook evidence of attendance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-415B: Beaufort official permission and instructions for copying Ascension plate. No Darwin receipt date or specific surviving request matched here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-439: Owen answers missing engagement announcement found on return last night, forwarding response through Darwin father because address unknown. No Darwin receipt date inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-473: Sends requested map and asks admission/time for a Tuesday lecture. Request medium unproved; no extant incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-499: Third-person library request for charts, not editorial paraphrase. Darwin-origin formal note remains grounding with no incoming.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-515: Thanks Mitchell for servant enquiries but says passage arranged after they met. Returns borrowed stone; later identification as tektite is not contemporary Darwin knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-560: Answers missing Milne enquiry about earthquakes and coincidence. Distinctive chance-coincidence warning is expressly acknowledged in562F. February20 date is editorial correction of older March dating, preserved in source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-557F: Asks Silliman forward enclosed Redfield letter556 and hopes earlier Journal gift reached him. Does not itself enclose the book. Later565 acknowledges book but never this covering request, so relationship remains possible, not confirmed reverse reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-562F: Milne acknowledges paper and explicitly thanks Darwin warning against coincident earthquakes, matching560. New Glen Almond phenomena and later inquiries are incoming voice only; event dates are not letter delivery.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-565: Silliman received Journal gift on April7 and had already read an imported copy. Does not mention557F or Redfield forwarding. Strong book-gift connection does not by itself identify a response to that letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-576: Questions originally written for Elizabeth Wedgwood, forwarded through Frances Allen to Smith. Smith answers survive as editorially recorded insertions, not Darwin voice or facts available on the outgoing circa-August15 date. Preserve intended and eventual recipient routes.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-578: Sends paper and reflects that his valuation of theory has changed since writing it. Requests future opinion rather than answering a located incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-580F: Belatedly acknowledges missing Smith communication; explains earlier Greaves paper already read June10 while Darwin away. Birds beaks received, but exact receipt and incoming text unlocated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-583: Fragment beginning mid-sentence about fungus and host-tree identification. Requests return of field notes; later correction belongs to591, not this earlier voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-591: Received Berkeley note and enclosure today, then corrects host tree from antarctica to betuloides. Neither incoming item survives here; Thursday in March remains a range, not an exact receipt day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-617: Requests support for Erasmus February7 ballot. Later success in Emma letter is not yet available knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-635: Provis supplies requested height data; missing Darwin request. Datum correction and omitted Bethesda location are incoming information, not activated on composition date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-636: Further Provis checking gives Tyn-y-maes as nearest measured point. Same-sender follow-up to635 is not a direct pair, and no intervening Darwin text survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-662A: Darwin report on Suttor manuscripts for RGS. Manuscripts are source material, not a surviving personal incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-666: Owen acknowledges missing condolence letter and reports bereavement and intended family visits. Susan letter to Caroline Owen is third-party; no Darwin delivery date established.
